title: Optical isomerism
examples: What makes a carbon atom chiral?
How do I know if a molecule has enantiomers?
Can you explain the difference between a chiral molecule and a racemate?

explain.say: Today we will learn about optical isomerism in chemistry.
A chiral centre is a carbon atom attached to four different groups.
If a molecule has a chiral centre, it can exist as enantiomers.
Enantiomers are non-superimposable mirror images of each other.
A racemate is an equal mixture of both enantiomers.
In real life, your hands are a perfect example of enantiomers.

faq.q: What is the difference between a chiral molecule and an achiral molecule?
faq.a: A chiral molecule has a chiral centre, meaning it is not superimposable on its mirror image. An achiral molecule has a plane of symmetry, so it matches its mirror image.
asks: How do I check for chirality?

faq.q: Do enantiomers have the same physical properties?
faq.a: They have the same properties except for how they interact with plane-polarized light. They rotate light in equal but opposite directions.
asks: Are they identical except for light?
What is the difference in physical properties?

faq.q: Why is a racemate often used in medicine?
faq.a: Sometimes, only one enantiomer is biologically active, but a racemate is used if both forms are needed or if separation is difficult.
asks: Is it always better to separate them?
What is the purpose of a racemate?

faq.q: If I draw a structure, how do I know if it has a chiral centre?
faq.a: You must check every carbon atom. If that carbon is attached to four groups that are all different, it is a chiral centre.
asks: How many groups must be different?
Can I just look at the carbon?

faq.q: What is the relationship between enantiomers and plane-polarized light?
faq.a: One enantiomer rotates light clockwise, which is called dextrorotatory. The other rotates it counter-clockwise, called levorotatory.
asks: Does one turn light right or left?

facts: A chiral centre is a carbon bonded to four different groups.
A racemate is a 50/50 mixture of both enantiomers.
The interaction with plane-polarized light is how enantiomers are distinguished.

quiz.say: Which condition defines a chiral centre?
quiz.show: Carbon bonded to four distinct groups

options.show: The molecule must contain a double bond.
options.say: The molecule must contain a double bond.

options.show: The carbon must be attached to four different atoms or groups.
options.say: The carbon must be attached to four different atoms or groups.

options.show: The carbon must be bonded to four atoms.
options.say: The carbon must be bonded to four atoms.

options.show: The molecule must show optical activity.
options.say: The molecule must show optical activity.

quiz.why: This definition ensures the molecule lacks symmetry, leading to chirality.

wrong.0: Double bonds do not automatically create a chiral centre.
wrong.2: This is too general; it does not specify that the four groups must be different.
wrong.3: Optical activity is a property, not the structural requirement for chirality.

quiz.say: If a molecule is a racemate, what does that mean for its enantiomers?

options.show: It means only one enantiomer is present.
options.say: It means only one enantiomer is present.

options.show: It means the enantiomers are chemically identical.
options.say: It means the enantiomers are chemically identical.

options.show: It contains exactly equal amounts of the two mirror-image forms.
options.say: It contains exactly equal amounts of the two mirror-image forms.

options.show: It means the molecule is achiral.
options.say: It means the molecule is achiral.

quiz.why: A 50/50 mix results in a net rotation of zero when tested with polarized light.

wrong.0: This describes a pure enantiomer, not a racemate.
wrong.1: They are structurally different, even if the mixture is balanced.
wrong.3: The molecule itself can still be chiral, but the mixture cancels out the optical activity.

quiz.say: If a molecule has a chiral centre, what pair of structures are possible?

options.show: It must form a meso compound.
options.say: It must form a meso compound.

options.show: It can exist as a pair of enantiomers.
options.say: It can exist as a pair of enantiomers.

options.show: It can only exist as a single structure.
options.say: It can only exist as a single structure.

quiz.why: The existence of a chiral centre dictates the potential for non-superimposable mirror images.

wrong.0: Meso compounds are achiral molecules that have internal symmetry.
wrong.2: This ignores the fundamental concept of stereoisomerism.
wrong.3: This is the opposite of the definition of a chiral centre.
